jobs.prompt:
Second Opus review of the auto-approve policy (tools/auto-approve-policy.mjs, hooks in tools/handbuild.mjs): FAIL. Fix all of these, one test each in tests/auto-approve.test.mjs, keep the other guard and approval tests passing; keep removing capability rather than parsing it.
1 HIGH normalizeGitRemoteUrl tries the scp-like pattern before scheme parsing, so an https or ssh URL to any host that ends in @TRUSTEDHOST:PATH normalises to the trusted URL, and bare or absolute local paths spelled host/path match. Parse by scheme first (https and ssh only, via URL); use the scp form only when there is no :// and no slash before the first colon; reject local or file paths, extra userinfo and non-default ports; compare scheme, host and path exactly against the canonical trusted value; http and https must not compare equal.
2 HIGH policy git runs and checks only hooksPath, pushurl, insteadOf and the origin push mapping. Config that runs programs or redirects traffic is unchecked: core.sshCommand, gpg.program with commit.gpgSign, core.fsmonitor (runs inside the hook during git status), filter drivers from gitattributes, core.pager and the editor, credential helpers, proxy settings, core.askPass. It can come from repo config or from the user's global gitconfig (HOME is kept). Fix: run every policy git query and the approved git command itself with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM pointed at /dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, and before granting or executing refuse when the repo config sets any of those keys (use git config --local --list and an allow-list of harmless keys: core.repositoryformatversion, core.filemode, core.bare, core.logallrefupdates, core.ignorecase, core.precomposeunicode, the origin url and fetch keys, the per-branch remote and merge keys, user.name, user.email); anything else refuses the auto-approval and falls back to the owner. Pass -c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.hooksPath=/nonexistent -c credential.helper= on policy runs.
3 MEDIUM-HIGH the hooks check looks at the git dir hooks, but linked worktrees run hooks from the shared common git dir: check git rev-parse --git-common-dir and the hooks directory there, and require core.hooksPath unset.
4 MEDIUM guardDecision makes a policy push free on policyGitInvocationRule alone, skipping the kill switch, shell/env check, rate limits and HEAD binding; make the push go through the same full policy check as every other op (no free path), and test that a push with the kill switch on or limits reached is not allowed.
5 MEDIUM Write, Edit and NotebookEdit under a policy window skip the kill switch, branch/HEAD binding and rate limits (only Bash goes through finishAllow), and the number of auto-approved windows per day is unlimited: route file-tool approvals through the same checks and add a per-day window cap.
6 MEDIUM the insteadOf and pushInsteadOf check can never match because git lowercases key names: lowercase the key before matching, and treat remote get-url --push --all expansion as the source of truth.
7 MEDIUM deleting stats.json resets the counters (a missing file reads as empty) and the files are protected only by exact path: protect the whole handbuild state folder from writes, deletes and renames in every mode, and treat a missing stats file as limit reached unless a fresh 'initialised' marker exists written by the policy itself.
8 MEDIUM scope too wide: remove job manifests under jobs and everything under coordination/review from the auto-approvable files.
9 LOW an empty granted HEAD disables the HEAD binding (deny instead); the push.default check can never run (drop it or make it run); the policy file path can be overridden by an environment variable (ignore the override unless the signed test marker exists); request-time checks run outside the lock (take the lock); a window with no git ops skips the per-op check; pick the window that covers the files, not the first live one; read-only git (status, diff, log) and git add are denied although the docs say allowed: allow them; anchor the SAFE_SWARM handbuild stats pattern.
